The remaining entries are zombie processes from my earlier service restarts. They have exited, so they are harmless, and nothing is still running.

The goal is met. `rust/` builds and passes its tests, and the service matches the original Java app on everything my comparison exercised.

## What was delivered

`/work/rust/` is a Cargo project (`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `src/`, no `target/`) that builds a single binary, `shogun-rest`. It reads `DATABASE_URL` and `PORT`, listens on `0.0.0.0`, and serves the six slice resources with the same behaviour as the original:

- **Auth:** HTTP Basic against `users`, bcrypt (`$2a$` only, as Spring's pattern requires), inactive users rejected, roles from users and groups, `ROLE_ADMIN` implying `ROLE_USER`.
- **Permissions:** the library's evaluators are rebuilt per entity class, including the own-user, group-member and always-read rules.
- **Writes:** ids from `hibernate_sequences` (`next_val + 1`, committed outside the request transaction), cascades in the original's order, collection replacement, and join-table writes.
- **Reads:** JSON shapes, `output:only` projections (including the original's HTTP 500 for data-source projections), filters, and sub-resources.

## How it was verified

- `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` pass, with and without `DATABASE_URL`. There are 15 tests: unit tests for the Jackson and Java conversions, plus an in-process HTTP test against a database that creates and removes its own fixture.
- I ran the original (`reference-app`) and my service side by side on identical seed data. The harness (`/work/harness/compare.py`, `scenarios.py`, outside the deliverable) replays 203 scenarios against both, comparing status, `WWW-Authenticate`, normalised JSON, and every slice table afterwards. All 203 match.

## Choices and limits

- **Error bodies:** the original returns Jetty's HTML error pages. I return empty bodies with the same status codes, so error-page bodies are not compared.
- **Set collapse:** the original's `equals` ignores ids, so detached members or roles with equal content collapse to the first one. The original's result can depend on whether two objects were created in the same millisecond. I always collapse, which matched every case I tested.
- **Partial writes:** a PUT with an unknown or badly typed property returns 404 but keeps the properties bound before it, as the original does.
- **XYZ resolutions:** non-empty arrays are refused as in the original (its Jackson binding fails). Stored values are read by decoding the Java-serialised double. Creation via REST is refused, as specified.
- **Fresh schema:** if `hibernate_sequences` has no `default` row, the service creates it and starts ids at 1. I did not verify this against the original, which would create its own row.
- **Connections:** id allocation uses a separate small pool, so a request transaction can never wait on an id allocation it is blocking.

I stopped the services I started and removed the `target/` directories I created (in `rust/` and in `reference/reference-app/`). `schema.sql` and `reference/` are otherwise untouched.

//! HTTP Basic authentication against the `users` table, and the entity
//! permission evaluators of the library (`de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.access`).

use std::collections::HashSet;

use base64::Engine;
use sqlx::Row;

use crate::model::Res;
use crate::store::{Conn, R};

pub const ROLE_ADMIN: &str = "ROLE_ADMIN";
pub const ROLE_USER: &str = "ROLE_USER";

/// The authenticated account: the user row and the roles it was granted.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Principal {
    pub id: i32,
    pub roles: HashSet<String>,
    pub is_admin: bool,
}

impl Principal {
    /// `hasRole('ROLE_USER')` with the role hierarchy ROLE_ADMIN > ROLE_USER.
    pub fn is_user_or_admin(&self) -> bool {
        self.is_admin || self.roles.contains(ROLE_USER)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Perm {
    Read,
    Update,
    Delete,
}

impl Perm {
    fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Perm::Read => "READ",
            Perm::Update => "UPDATE",
            Perm::Delete => "DELETE",
        }
    }
}

/// Which permission evaluator of the library applies to an entity class.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind {
    /// `PersistentObjectPermissionEvaluator`: explicit permissions only.
    Standard,
    /// `AlwaysAllowReadPermissionEvaluator`: READ for everyone.
    AlwaysRead,
    /// `UserPermissionEvaluator`: READ of the own user.
    User,
    /// `UserGroupPermissionEvaluator`: READ for the members.
    Group,
}

pub fn kind_of(r: Res) -> Kind {
    match r {
        Res::Users => Kind::User,
        Res::Groups => Kind::Group,
        Res::Layers => Kind::Standard,
        Res::Roles | Res::DataSources | Res::Appearances => Kind::AlwaysRead,
    }
}

/// The BCrypt pattern Spring's encoder checks before comparing.
fn looks_like_bcrypt(enc: &str) -> bool {
    let b = enc.as_bytes();
    if b.len() != 60 {
        return false;
    }
    let prefix_ok = enc.starts_with("$2a$") || enc.starts_with("$2$");
    if !prefix_ok {
        return false;
    }
    let rest = if enc.starts_with("$2a$") { &b[4..] } else { &b[3..] };
    if rest.len() < 3 || !rest[0].is_ascii_digit() || !rest[1].is_ascii_digit() || rest[2] != b'$' {
        return false;
    }
    rest[3..]
        .iter()
        .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || *c == b'.' || *c == b'/')
}

fn bcrypt_matches(raw: &str, enc: &str) -> bool {
    if !looks_like_bcrypt(enc) {
        return false;
    }
    bcrypt::verify(raw, enc).unwrap_or(false)
}

/// Basic authentication as the original's filter chain does it. `None` is a 401.
pub async fn authenticate(c: &mut Conn, auth_header: Option<&str>) -> R<Option<Principal>> {
    let header = match auth_header {
        Some(h) => h,
        None => return Ok(None),
    };
    let encoded = match header.get(..6) {
        Some(p) if p.eq_ignore_ascii_case("basic ") => header[6..].trim(),
        _ => return Ok(None),
    };
    let decoded = match base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.decode(encoded) {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(_) => return Ok(None),
    };
    let decoded = match String::from_utf8(decoded) {
        Ok(s) => s,
        Err(_) => return Ok(None),
    };
    let (account, raw_password) = match decoded.split_once(':') {

/// (`hasPermission(entity, perm)`). Admins pass every check.
pub async fn has_perm(c: &mut Conn, p: &Principal, kind: Kind, entity_id: i32, perm: Perm) -> R<bool> {
    if p.is_admin {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    if perm == Perm::Read {
        match kind {
            Kind::AlwaysRead => return Ok(true),
            Kind::User if entity_id == p.id => return Ok(true),
            Kind::Group => {
                let member: Option<i32> = sqlx::query_scalar(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM user_usergroup WHERE user_id = $1 AND usergroup_id = $2",
                )
                .bind(p.id)
                .bind(entity_id)
                .fetch_optional(&mut *c)
                .await?;
                if member.is_some() {
                    return Ok(true);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let perms: Vec<Option<String>> = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT pp.permissions FROM userpermissions up \
         JOIN permissioncollections_permissions pp ON pp.permissioncollections_id = up.userpermissions_id \
         WHERE up.entity_id = $1 AND up.userpermissions_key = $2 \
         UNION ALL \
         SELECT pp.permissions FROM grouppermissions gp \
         JOIN permissioncollections_permissions pp ON pp.permissioncollections_id = gp.grouppermissions_id \
         WHERE gp.entity_id = $1 AND gp.grouppermissions_key IN \
           (SELECT ug.usergroup_id FROM user_usergroup ug WHERE ug.user_id = $2)",
    )
    .bind(entity_id)
    .bind(p.id)
    .fetch_all(&mut *c)
    .await?;
    Ok(perms
        .iter()
        .flatten()
        .any(|s| s == perm.name() || s == "ADMIN"))
}

/// The same check on the bean of a restricted (projection) query. Those beans
/// are default-constructed: they carry no permissions and no members, and the
/// own-user test never matches, so only the always-readable kinds pass.
pub fn bean_has_perm(p: &Principal, kind: Kind, perm: Perm) -> bool {
    if p.is_admin {
        return true;
    }
    perm == Perm::Read && kind == Kind::AlwaysRead
}

//! applies when binding request bodies, and the Java `toString` formats that
//! the original stores in text columns.

use chrono::NaiveDate;
use serde_json::{Map, Number, Value};

/// A JSON binding failure. The original's Jackson raises an exception here;
/// the controller turns it into a status code, so the detail is only logged.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct JErr(pub String);

pub type JResult<T> = Result<T, JErr>;

pub fn err<T>(msg: impl Into<String>) -> JResult<T> {
    Err(JErr(msg.into()))
}

/// Integer property (`Integer`, nullable): null stays null.
pub fn int_opt(v: &Value) -> JResult<Option<i32>> {
    match v {
        Value::Null => Ok(None),
        Value::Number(n) => {
            if let Some(i) = n.as_i64() {
                i32::try_from(i).map(Some).or_else(|_| err("int overflow"))
            } else if let Some(f) = n.as_f64() {
                // Jackson accepts floats for ints and truncates them.
                if f.is_finite() && f.abs() < i32::MAX as f64 {
                    Ok(Some(f.trunc() as i32))
                } else {
                    err("int overflow")
                }
            } else {
                err("int")
            }
        }
        Value::String(s) => {
            let t = s.trim();
            if t.is_empty() {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            t.parse::<i32>().map(Some).or_else(|_| err("not an int"))
        }
        _ => err("not an int"),
    }
}

/// Primitive `int`: null becomes 0.
pub fn int_prim(v: &Value) -> JResult<i32> {
    Ok(int_opt(v)?.unwrap_or(0))
}

/// Boolean wrapper: null stays null; numbers are non-zero, strings must be true/false.
pub fn bool_opt(v: &Value) -> JResult<Option<bool>> {
    match v {
        Value::Null => Ok(None),
        Value::Bool(b) => Ok(Some(*b)),
        Value::Number(n) => Ok(Some(n.as_f64().map(|f| f != 0.0).unwrap_or(false))),
        Value::String(s) => match s.as_str() {
            "true" | "True" | "TRUE" => Ok(Some(true)),
            "false" | "False" | "FALSE" | "" => Ok(Some(false)),
            _ => err("not a boolean"),
        },
        _ => err("not a boolean"),
    }
}

fn is_parsable(s: &str) -> bool {
    if s.is_empty() || s.ends_with('.') {
        return false;
    }
    let body = if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix('-') {
        if rest.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        rest
    } else {
        s
    };
    let mut dots = 0;
    for ch in body.chars() {
        if ch == '.' {
            dots += 1;
            if dots > 1 {
                return false;
            }
        } else if !ch.is_ascii_digit() {
            return false;
        }
    }
    true

pub fn property_from_db(s: &str) -> Value {
    if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("true") {
        return Value::Bool(true);
    }
    if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("false") {
        return Value::Bool(false);
    }
    if is_parsable(s) {
        if is_digits(s) || (s.starts_with('-') && is_digits(&s[1..])) {
            if let Ok(l) = s.parse::<i64>() {
                return Value::Number(Number::from(l));

        Value::Bool(b) => Ok(b.to_string()),
        Value::String(s) => Ok(s.clone()),
        Value::Number(n) => {
            if let Some(i) = n.as_i64() {

            } else {
                Ok(java_double(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0)))
            }
        }
        other => Ok(java_tostring(other)),
    }

/// Java's `toString()` of the Map/List/scalar values Jackson builds.
pub fn java_tostring(v: &Value) -> String {
    match v {
        Value::Null => "null".to_string(),
        Value::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),
        Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
        Value::Number(n) => match n.as_i64() {
            Some(i) => i.to_string(),
            None => java_double(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0)),
        },
        Value::Array(a) => {
            let parts: Vec<String> = a.iter().map(java_tostring).collect();
            format!("[{}]", parts.join(", "))
        }
        Value::Object(m) => {
            let parts: Vec<String> = m
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| format!("{}={}", k, java_tostring(v)))
                .collect();
            format!("{{{}}}", parts.join(", "))
        }
    }
}

/// `Double.toString(d)`.
pub fn java_double(d: f64) -> String {
    if d.is_nan() {
        return "NaN".into();
    }
    if d.is_infinite() {
        return if d > 0.0 { "Infinity".into() } else { "-Infinity".into() };
    }
    if d == 0.0 {
        return if d.is_sign_negative() { "-0.0".into() } else { "0.0".into() };
    }
    // Shortest round-trip digits and exponent, from Rust's `{:e}`.
    let sci = format!("{:e}", d.abs());
    let (mant, exp) = sci.split_once('e').unwrap();
    let exp: i32 = exp.parse().unwrap();
    let digits: String = mant.chars().filter(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).collect();
    let sign = if d < 0.0 { "-" } else { "" };
    let abs = d.abs();
    if (1e-3..1e7).contains(&abs) {
        // plain decimal notation
        let point = exp + 1; // digits before the decimal point
        let mut out = String::new();
        if point <= 0 {
            out.push_str("0.");
            for _ in 0..(-point) {
                out.push('0');
            }
            out.push_str(&digits);
        } else {
            let p = point as usize;
            if digits.len() <= p {
                out.push_str(&digits);
                for _ in 0..(p - digits.len()) {
                    out.push('0');
                }
                out.push_str(".0");
            } else {
                out.push_str(&digits[..p]);
                out.push('.');
                out.push_str(&digits[p..]);
            }
        }
        format!("{}{}", sign, out)
    } else {
        let first = &digits[..1];
        let rest = if digits.len() > 1 { &digits[1..] } else { "0" };
        format!("{}{}.{}E{}", sign, first, rest, exp)
    }

/// A `HashSet` of detached objects: an element equal to an earlier one (by the
/// library's `equals`, which ignores the id) is dropped; the first one stays.
fn dedupe_by<T>(items: Vec<T>, key: impl Fn(&T) -> String) -> Vec<T> {
    let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    items.into_iter().filter(|t| seen.insert(key(t))).collect()

        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn apply_kind(&mut self, k: &str, v: &Value) -> JResult<()> {
        match &mut self.kind {
            DsKind::ImageWms(i) => i.apply(k, v),
            DsKind::TileWms(t) => match k {
                "tileGrid" => {
                    t.tile_grid = TileGrid::from_json(v, false)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "requestWithTiled" => {
                    t.request_with_tiled = bool_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => t.image.apply(k, v),
            },
            DsKind::Wfs(w) => match k {
                "version" => {
                    w.version = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "typeName" => {
                    w.type_name = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "typeNames" => {
                    w.type_names = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => err(format!("unknown property {k} on WfsLayerDataSource")),
            },
            DsKind::Wmts(w) => match k {
                "tileGrid" => {
                    w.tile_grid = TileGrid::from_json(v, true)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "urls" => {
                    w.urls = str_list(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "wmtsLayer" => {
                    w.wmts_layer = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "wmtsStyle" => {
                    w.wmts_style = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "projection" => {

                    Ok(())

                "matrixSet" => {
                    w.matrix_set = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "requestEncoding" => {
                    w.request_encoding = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "capabilitiesUrl" => {
                    w.capabilities_url = string_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => err(format!("unknown property {k} on WmtsLayerDataSource")),
            },
            DsKind::Xyz(x) => match k {
                "center" => {
                    x.center = Point::from_json(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "extent" => {
                    x.extent = Extent::from_json(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "resolutions" => {
                    // Jackson binds the elements as Point2D.Double, so a non-empty
                    // array cannot be read (null and [] are fine)
                    if let Value::Array(a) = v {
                        if !a.is_empty() {
                            return err("cannot construct Point2D.Double from a number");
                        }
                    }
                    x.resolutions = f64_list(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                "tileSize" => {
                    x.tile_size = int_opt(v)?;
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => err(format!("unknown property {k} on XyzLayerDataSource")),
            },
        }
    }

    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
        let mut m = Map::new();
        m.insert("id".into(), opt_i32(&self.id));
        m.insert("name".into(), opt_str(&self.name));
        m.insert("type".into(), opt_str(&self.type_));
        m.insert("url".into(), opt_str(&self.url));
        m.insert("format".into(), opt_str(&self.format));
        match &self.kind {
            DsKind::ImageWms(i) => i.write_json(&mut m),
            DsKind::TileWms(t) => {
                t.image.write_json(&mut m);
                m.insert("tileGrid".into(), tile_grid_json(&t.tile_grid));
                m.insert("requestWithTiled".into(), opt_bool(&t.request_with_tiled));
            }
            DsKind::Wfs(w) => {
                m.insert("version".into(), opt_str(&w.version));
                m.insert("typeName".into(), opt_str(&w.type_name));
                m.insert("typeNames".into(), opt_str(&w.type_names));
            }
            DsKind::Wmts(w) => {
                m.insert("tileGrid".into(), tile_grid_json(&w.tile_grid));
                m.insert("urls".into(), vec_json(&w.urls, |s| Value::String(s.clone())));
                m.insert("wmtsLayer".into(), opt_str(&w.wmts_layer));
                m.insert("wmtsStyle".into(), opt_str(&w.wmts_style));
                m.insert("projection".into(), opt_str(&w.projection));
                m.insert("matrixSet".into(), opt_str(&w.matrix_set));
                m.insert("requestEncoding".into(), opt_str(&w.request_encoding));
                m.insert("capabilitiesUrl".into(), opt_str(&w.capabilities_url));
            }
            DsKind::Xyz(x) => {
                m.insert("center".into(), point_json(&x.center));
                m.insert("extent".into(), extent_json(&x.extent));
                m.insert("resolutions".into(), vec_json(&x.resolutions, |d| f64_val(*d)));
                m.insert("tileSize".into(), opt_i32(&x.tile_size));

        Value::Object(m)
    }

/// Converts a query-string value the way ConvertUtils does for the field type
/// (bad numbers become 0, bad booleans become false).
pub fn convert_query_value(t: FType, s: &str) -> Cell {
    match t {
        FType::Str => Cell::Str(Some(s.to_string())),
        FType::Int => Cell::Int(Some(s.trim().parse::<i32>().unwrap_or(0))),
        FType::Dbl => Cell::Dbl(Some(s.trim().parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(0.0))),

fn split_list(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let pieces: Vec<&str> = s.split(',').collect();
    let n = pieces.len();
    let mut out: Vec<String> = pieces
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, p)| {

            if i > 0 {

            }
            if i + 1 < n {

fn restrict_fields(query: &[(String, String)], res: Res) -> Option<Vec<&'static str>> {

        .fields()
        .iter()
        .map(|(f, _)| *f)
        .filter(|f| requested.iter().any(|r| r.eq_ignore_ascii_case(f)))
        .collect();

        .iter()
        .filter(|p| p.0 != "output:only")

        let first_key: Option<String> = non_restrict

pub async fn handle(State(st): State<Arc<AppState>>, req: Request) -> Response {

    let method = if parts.method == Method::HEAD { Method::GET } else { parts.method.clone() };

    let headers: HeaderMap = parts.headers.clone();

        Some(p) if p.is_empty() || p.starts_with('/') => p.to_string(),
        _ => return not_found(),
    };
    let segs: Vec<String> = rest_path
        .split('/')
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .map(|s| s.to_string())
        .collect();

    let body_bytes = match axum::body::to_bytes(body, 64 * 1024 * 1024).await {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(_) => return bad_request(),
    };

    let mut conn = match st.pool.acquire().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return internal(),
    };
    let auth_header = headers
        .get(header::AUTHORIZATION)
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok());
    let principal = match auth::authenticate(&mut conn, auth_header).await {
        Ok(Some(p)) => p,
        Ok(None) => return unauthorized(),
        Err(_) => return internal(),
    };
    drop(conn);

        .map(|(k, v)| (k.into_owned(), v.into_owned()))
        .collect();

    let in_slice = SLICE.contains(&slice_seg);
    // the security rules: slice paths need ROLE_USER, every other /rest path ROLE_ADMIN
    if in_slice {
        if !principal.is_user_or_admin() {
            return status_only(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN);
        }
    } else if !principal.is_admin {
        return status_only(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN);
    }

        Some(r) if in_slice => r,
        _ => return not_found(),

            Method::GET => list(st, &principal, res, &query).await,

                Method::PUT => update(st, &principal, res, id, &body_bytes).await,

async fn run_list(st: &AppState, p: &Principal, res: Res, query: &[(String, String)], is_filter: bool) -> Response {

    let conds = if is_filter {
        let c = filter_conditions(query, res);
        if c.is_empty() {

        }
        Some(c)

        Err(_) => return internal(),

        Err(_) => return internal(),
    };
    let matched: Vec<Ent> = match &conds {
        Some(c) => all.into_iter().filter(|e| matches_conditions(e, c)).collect(),
        None => all,
    };
    let kind = kind_of(res);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    match restrict {
        None => {
            for e in matched {
                let id = match e.id() {
                    Some(i) => i,
                    None => continue,
                };
                match has_perm(&mut conn, p, kind, id, Perm::Read).await {
                    Ok(true) => out.push(e.to_json()),
                    Ok(false) => {}
                    Err(_) => return internal(),
                }
            }
        }
        Some(fields) => {
            // the abstract LayerDataSource cannot be instantiated for a projection
            if res == Res::DataSources {
                return if matched.is_empty() {
                    json_response(StatusCode::OK, &json!([]))
                } else {
                    internal()
                };
            }
            for e in matched {
                if bean_has_perm(p, kind, Perm::Read) {
                    out.push(restricted_json(res, &e, &fields));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    json_response(StatusCode::OK, &Value::Array(out))

fn parse_body(body: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Value>, ()> {
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(body);
    if text.trim().is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let mut stream = serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(&text).into_iter::<Value>();
    match stream.next() {
        Some(Ok(v)) => Ok(Some(v)),
        _ => Err(()),
    }

/// Jackson's `asInt()` on the payload's "id" node.
fn payload_int(v: &Value) -> i32 {
    match v {
        Value::Number(n) => n.as_i64().map(|i| i as i32).or_else(|| n.as_f64().map(|f| f as i32)).unwrap_or(0),
        Value::String(s) => s.trim().parse::<i32>().unwrap_or(0),
        Value::Bool(b) => i32::from(*b),
        _ => 0,
    }
}

async fn update(st: &AppState, p: &Principal, res: Res, id: i32, body: &[u8]) -> Response {
    // a malformed body fails in readTree (404); an empty one yields no node (400)
    let value = match parse_body(body) {
        Ok(Some(v)) => v,
        Ok(None) => return bad_request(),
        Err(()) => return not_found(),
    };
    let payload = match value.as_object().and_then(|m| m.get("id")) {
        Some(idv) => idv.clone(),
        None => return bad_request(),
    };
    if payload_int(&payload) != id {
        return bad_request();
    }
    let map: &Map<String, Value> = match value.as_object() {
        Some(m) => m,
        None => return bad_request(),
    };

    let mut tx = match st.pool.begin().await {
        Ok(t) => t,
        Err(_) => return internal(),
    };
    let orig = match load_ent(&mut tx, res, id).await {
        Ok(Some(e)) => e,
        Ok(None) => {
            let _ = tx.rollback().await;
            return not_found();
        }
        Err(_) => {
            let _ = tx.rollback().await;
            return not_found();
        }
    };
    let kind = kind_of(res);
    // findById (READ) and updatePartialWithJsonNode (UPDATE)
    let readable = has_perm(&mut tx, p, kind, id, Perm::Read).await;
    let updatable = has_perm(&mut tx, p, kind, id, Perm::Update).await;
    if !matches!(readable, Ok(true)) || !matches!(updatable, Ok(true)) {
        let _ = tx.rollback().await;
        return not_found();
    }

    let mut ent = orig.clone();
    let mut touched = Touched::default();
    let mut json_failed = false;
    for (k, v) in map {
        if is_ignored_prop(k) {
            continue;
        }
        if ent.apply(k, v).is_err() {
            // Jackson fails midway: the properties bound so far are still flushed
            json_failed = true;
            break;
        }
        if let Some(tk) = touched_key(k) {
            touched.0.insert(tk);

    if let Err(e) = save_update(&mut tx, &st.ids, &mut ent, &orig, &touched).await {
        eprintln!("update {res:?}/{id} rolled back: {}", e.describe());
        let _ = tx.rollback().await;
        return not_found();
    }
    if let Err(e) = tx.commit().await {
        eprintln!("update {res:?}/{id} commit failed: {e}");
        return not_found();
    }

        return not_found();
    }
    json_response(StatusCode::OK, &ent.to_json())

/// transaction on its own pool, so an id stays used even if the request fails.
pub async fn next_id(ids: &PgPool) -> R<i32> {
    let v: Option<i64> = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "UPDATE hibernate_sequences SET next_val = next_val + 1 \
         WHERE sequence_name = 'default' RETURNING next_val",
    )
    .fetch_optional(ids)
    .await?;
    match v {
        Some(v) => Ok(v as i32),
        None => {

            let v: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
                "INSERT INTO hibernate_sequences (sequence_name, next_val) VALUES ('default', 1) \
                 ON CONFLICT (sequence_name) DO UPDATE \
                 SET next_val = hibernate_sequences.next_val + 1 RETURNING next_val",
            )
            .fetch_one(ids)
            .await?;
            Ok(v as i32)
        }
    }

fn dedupe_by_id<T>(v: Vec<(Option<i32>, T)>) -> R<Vec<T>> {
    // A HashSet of detached objects: equal ids collapse onto the first one.
    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (id, t) in v {
        let id = match id {
            Some(i) => i,
            None => return bad("transient object in collection"),
        };
        if seen.insert(id) {
            out.push(t);
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Writes an appearance. `nested` objects always replace their properties.
pub async fn save_appearance(
    c: &mut Conn,
    ids: &PgPool,
    a: &mut Appearance,
    original_id: Option<i32>,
    nested: bool,
    touched: &Touched,
) -> R<()> {
    let is_new = a.id.is_none();
    if is_new {
        let id = next_id(ids).await?;
        a.id = Some(id);
        sqlx::query(
            "INSERT INTO layerappearances (id, created, modified, attribution, clickable, \
             hovertemplate, hoverable, maxresolution, minresolution, name, opacity, visible) \
             VALUES ($1, localtimestamp, localtimestamp, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9, $10)",
        )
        .bind(a.id)
        .bind(&a.attribution)
        .bind(a.clickable)
        .bind(&a.hover_template)
        .bind(a.hoverable)
        .bind(a.max_resolution)
        .bind(a.min_resolution)
        .bind(&a.name)
        .bind(a.opacity)
        .bind(a.visible)
        .execute(&mut *c)
        .await?;
    } else {
        let id = check_id(a.id)?;
        if nested && original_id == Some(id) {
            // The original session already holds this instance.
            return bad("NonUniqueObjectException");
        }
        let res = sqlx::query(
            "UPDATE layerappearances SET modified = localtimestamp, attribution = $2, \
             clickable = $3, hovertemplate = $4, hoverable = $5, maxresolution = $6, \
             minresolution = $7, name = $8, opacity = $9, visible = $10 WHERE id = $1",
        )
        .bind(id)
        .bind(&a.attribution)
        .bind(a.clickable)
        .bind(&a.hover_template)
        .bind(a.hoverable)
        .bind(a.max_resolution)
        .bind(a.min_resolution)
        .bind(&a.name)
        .bind(a.opacity)
        .bind(a.visible)
        .execute(&mut *c)
        .await?;
        expect_one(res).await?;
    }
    let id = check_id(a.id)?;
    if is_new || nested || touched.has("properties") {
        sqlx::query("DELETE FROM layerappearances_properties WHERE appearance_id = $1")
            .bind(id)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
        if let Some(props) = &a.properties {
            for (k, v) in props {
                // a null map value is not written (no row for it)
                if v.is_null() {
                    continue;
                }
                let db = property_to_db(v)?;
                sqlx::query(
                    "INSERT INTO layerappearances_properties (appearance_id, property, value) \
                     VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
                )
                .bind(id)
                .bind(k)
                .bind(db)
                .execute(&mut *c)
                .await?;
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Saves a tile grid as a cascaded (nested) object: always written in full.
/// `orig_tg` / `orig_ext` are the ids the original session already holds.
pub async fn save_tile_grid(
    c: &mut Conn,
    ids: &PgPool,
    t: &mut TileGrid,
    orig_tg: Option<i32>,
    orig_ext: Option<i32>,
) -> R<()> {
    let is_new = t.id.is_none();
    if is_new {
        // parent first: the id is allocated before the extent cascade
        let id = next_id(ids).await?;
        t.id = Some(id);
    } else if orig_tg == t.id {
        return bad("NonUniqueObjectException");
    }
    if let Some(e) = t.extent.as_mut() {
        save_extent(c, ids, e, orig_ext, true).await?;
    }
    let id = check_id(t.id)?;
    let ext_id = t.extent.as_ref().and_then(|e| e.id);
    let origin = t.origin.clone();
    if is_new {
        sqlx::query(
            "INSERT INTO tilegrids (id, created, modified, tilegridorigin_x, tilegridorigin_y, \
             tilesize, type, tilegridextent_id) \
             VALUES ($1, localtimestamp, localtimestamp, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)",
        )
        .bind(id)
        .bind(origin.as_ref().map(|p| p.x))
        .bind(origin.as_ref().map(|p| p.y))
        .bind(t.tile_size)
        .bind(&t.type_)
        .bind(ext_id)
        .execute(&mut *c)
        .await?;
        if t.wmts {
            sqlx::query("INSERT INTO wmtstilegrids (id) VALUES ($1)")
                .bind(id)
                .execute(&mut *c)
                .await?;
        }
    } else {
        let res = sqlx::query(
            "UPDATE tilegrids SET modified = localtimestamp, tilegridorigin_x = $2, \
             tilegridorigin_y = $3, tilesize = $4, type = $5, tilegridextent_id = $6 WHERE id = $1",
        )
        .bind(id)
        .bind(origin.as_ref().map(|p| p.x))
        .bind(origin.as_ref().map(|p| p.y))
        .bind(t.tile_size)
        .bind(&t.type_)
        .bind(ext_id)
        .execute(&mut *c)
        .await?;
        expect_one(res).await?;
    }
    // element collections of a detached object are always recreated
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM tilegrid_resolution WHERE tilegrid_id = $1")
        .bind(id)
        .execute(&mut *c)
        .await?;
    if let Some(res) = &t.resolutions {
        for (idx, r) in res.iter().enumerate() {
            sqlx::query(
                "INSERT INTO tilegrid_resolution (tilegrid_id, resolution, idx) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
            )
            .bind(id)
            .bind(*r)
            .bind(idx as i32)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
        }
    }
    if t.wmts {
        sqlx::query("DELETE FROM wmtstilegrids_matrixids WHERE wmtstilegrids_id = $1")
            .bind(id)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
        if let Some(ids) = &t.matrix_ids {
            for m in ids {
                sqlx::query(
                    "INSERT INTO wmtstilegrids_matrixids (wmtstilegrids_id, matrixids) VALUES ($1, $2)",
                )
                .bind(id)
                .bind(m)
                .execute(&mut *c)
                .await?;
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Writes the entity behind an update of a managed data source.
pub async fn update_ds(
    c: &mut Conn,
    ids: &PgPool,
    d: &mut DataSource,
    orig: &DataSource,
    touched: &Touched,
) -> R<()> {
    let id = check_id(d.id)?;
    let res = sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE layerdatasources SET modified = localtimestamp, format = $2, name = $3, \
         type = $4, url = $5 WHERE id = $1",
    )
    .bind(id)
    .bind(&d.format)
    .bind(&d.name)
    .bind(&d.type_)
    .bind(&d.url)
    .execute(&mut *c)
    .await?;
    expect_one(res).await?;
    let orig_tg = match &orig.kind {
        DsKind::TileWms(t) => t.tile_grid.as_ref().and_then(|g| g.id),
        DsKind::Wmts(w) => w.tile_grid.as_ref().and_then(|g| g.id),
        _ => None,
    };
    let orig_ext = match &orig.kind {
        DsKind::TileWms(t) => t.tile_grid.as_ref().and_then(|g| g.extent.as_ref()).and_then(|e| e.id),
        DsKind::Wmts(w) => w.tile_grid.as_ref().and_then(|g| g.extent.as_ref()).and_then(|e| e.id),
        _ => None,
    };
    match &mut d.kind {
        DsKind::ImageWms(i) => update_image(c, id, i).await?,
        DsKind::TileWms(t) => {
            if touched.has("tileGrid") {
                if let Some(tg) = t.tile_grid.as_mut() {
                    save_tile_grid(c, ids, tg, orig_tg, orig_ext).await?;
                }
            }
            update_image(c, id, &t.image).await?;
            let tg_id = t.tile_grid.as_ref().and_then(|g| g.id);
            let res = sqlx::query(
                "UPDATE tilewmslayerdatasources SET request_with_tiled = $2, tilegrid_id = $3 WHERE id = $1",
            )
            .bind(id)
            .bind(t.request_with_tiled)
            .bind(tg_id)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
            expect_one(res).await?;
        }
        DsKind::Wfs(w) => {
            let res = sqlx::query(
                "UPDATE wfslayerdatasources SET typename = $2, typenames = $3, version = $4 WHERE id = $1",
            )
            .bind(id)
            .bind(&w.type_name)
            .bind(&w.type_names)
            .bind(&w.version)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
            expect_one(res).await?;
        }
        DsKind::Wmts(w) => {
            if touched.has("tileGrid") {
                if let Some(tg) = w.tile_grid.as_mut() {
                    save_tile_grid(c, ids, tg, orig_tg, orig_ext).await?;
                }
            }
            let tg_id = w.tile_grid.as_ref().and_then(|g| g.id);
            let res = sqlx::query(
                "UPDATE wmtslayerdatasources SET capabilitiesurl = $2, matrixset = $3, projection = $4, \
                 requestencoding = $5, wmtslayer = $6, wmtsstyle = $7, tilegrid_id = $8 WHERE id = $1",
            )
            .bind(id)
            .bind(&w.capabilities_url)
            .bind(&w.matrix_set)
            .bind(&w.projection)
            .bind(&w.request_encoding)
            .bind(&w.wmts_layer)
            .bind(&w.wmts_style)
            .bind(tg_id)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
            expect_one(res).await?;
            if touched.has("urls") {
                sqlx::query("DELETE FROM wmtslayerdatasources_urls WHERE wmtslayerdatasources_id = $1")
                    .bind(id)
                    .execute(&mut *c)
                    .await?;
                if let Some(urls) = &w.urls {
                    for u in urls {
                        sqlx::query(
                            "INSERT INTO wmtslayerdatasources_urls (wmtslayerdatasources_id, urls) VALUES ($1, $2)",
                        )
                        .bind(id)
                        .bind(u)
                        .execute(&mut *c)
                        .await?;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        DsKind::Xyz(x) => {
            let ext_id = match x.extent.as_mut() {
                // no cascade: the extent must exist already
                Some(e) => Some(check_id(e.id)?),
                None => None,
            };
            let res = sqlx::query(
                "UPDATE xyzlayerdatasources SET center_x = $2, center_y = $3, tilesize = $4, \
                 extent_id = $5 WHERE id = $1",
            )
            .bind(id)
            .bind(x.center.as_ref().map(|p| p.x))
            .bind(x.center.as_ref().map(|p| p.y))
            .bind(x.tile_size)
            .bind(ext_id)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
            expect_one(res).await?;
            if touched.has("resolutions") {
                sqlx::query("DELETE FROM xyzlayerdatasrc_resolution WHERE xyzlayerdatasrc_id = $1")
                    .bind(id)
                    .execute(&mut *c)
                    .await?;
                if let Some(res) = &x.resolutions {
                    for (idx, r) in res.iter().enumerate() {
                        sqlx::query(
                            "INSERT INTO xyzlayerdatasrc_resolution (xyzlayerdatasrc_id, resolution, idx) \
                             VALUES ($1, $2, $3)",
                        )
                        .bind(id)
                        .bind(encode_java_double(*r))
                        .bind(idx as i32)
                        .execute(&mut *c)
                        .await?;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Removes the first occurrence of the layer from a map's ordered layer list
/// and renumbers the list, as Hibernate does for an indexed collection.
pub async fn remove_layer_from_map(c: &mut Conn, map_id: i32, layer_id: i32) -> R<()> {
    let mut layers: Vec<i32> = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT layer_id FROM maps_layers WHERE map_id = $1 ORDER BY idx",
    )
    .bind(map_id)
    .fetch_all(&mut *c)
    .await?;
    if let Some(pos) = layers.iter().position(|l| *l == layer_id) {
        layers.remove(pos);
    }
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM maps_layers WHERE map_id = $1")
        .bind(map_id)
        .execute(&mut *c)
        .await?;
    for (idx, l) in layers.iter().enumerate() {
        sqlx::query("INSERT INTO maps_layers (map_id, layer_id, idx) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)")
            .bind(map_id)
            .bind(l)
            .bind(idx as i32)
            .execute(&mut *c)
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

async fn http_flow_against_a_database() {
    use axum::Router;
    use axum::body::Body;
    use axum::http::{Request, StatusCode, header};
    use base64::Engine;
    use sqlx::postgres::PgPoolOptions;
    use std::sync::Arc;

        None => {

            return;
        }
    };
    let pool = PgPoolOptions::new().max_connections(4).connect(&url).await.expect("connect");
    let ids = PgPoolOptions::new().max_connections(2).connect(&url).await.expect("connect");
    let state = Arc::new(crate::rest::AppState { pool: pool.clone(), ids: ids.clone() });

    // A plain user with ROLE_USER, created here and removed at the end.
    let role_id: Option<i32> = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM roles WHERE name = 'ROLE_USER'")
        .fetch_optional(&pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let (role_id, created_role) = match role_id {
        Some(r) => (r, false),
        None => {
            let r = crate::store::next_id(&ids).await.unwrap();
            sqlx::query("INSERT INTO roles (id, created, modified, name) VALUES ($1, now(), now(), 'ROLE_USER')")
                .bind(r)
                .execute(&pool)
                .await
                .unwrap();
            (r, true)
        }
    };
    let account = format!("unit-{}", std::process::id());
    let user_id = crate::store::next_id(&ids).await.unwrap();
    // Spring's BCrypt pattern only accepts the $2a$ form
    let hash = bcrypt::hash_with_result("unit-pw", 4)
        .unwrap()
        .format_for_version(bcrypt::Version::TwoA);
    sqlx::query("INSERT INTO persons (id, created, modified, firstname) VALUES ($1, now(), now(), 'Unit')")
        .bind(user_id)
        .execute(&pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    sqlx::query("INSERT INTO users (id, accountname, active, password) VALUES ($1, $2, true, $3)")
        .bind(user_id)
        .bind(&account)
        .bind(&hash)
        .execute(&pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    sqlx::query("INSERT INTO users_roles (user_id, role_id) VALUES ($1, $2)")
        .bind(user_id)
        .bind(role_id)
        .execute(&pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();

    let app = Router::new().fallback(crate::rest::handle).with_state(state);
    let auth = format!(
        "Basic {}",
        base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(format!("{account}:unit-pw"))
    );
    let call = |method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>, with_auth: bool| {
        let mut b = Request::builder().method(method).uri(path);
        if with_auth {
            b = b.header(header::AUTHORIZATION, auth.clone());
        }
        let body = match body {
            Some(s) => Body::from(s.to_string()),
            None => Body::empty(),
        };
        app.clone().oneshot(b.body(body).unwrap())
    };

    // authentication
    let resp = call("GET", "/rest/roles", None, false).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(resp.status(), StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
    assert!(resp.headers().get(header::WWW_AUTHENTICATE).is_some());

    assert_eq!(resp.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let bytes = axum::body::to_bytes(resp.into_body(), usize::MAX).await.unwrap();
    let roles: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap();
    assert!(roles.as_array().unwrap().iter().any(|r| r["name"] == "ROLE_USER"));

    let resp = call("GET", &format!("/rest/users/{user_id}"), None, true).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(resp.status(), StatusCode::OK);

    if created_role {
        sqlx::query("DELETE FROM roles WHERE id = $1").bind(role_id).execute(&pool).await.unwrap();
    }
}
